newsitem.title: USA: Probation for NY man who stole jewels from Fergie.
newsitem.headline: Probation for NY man who stole jewels from Fergie.

text.p: An airport baggage handler was sentenced to four years probation on Friday for stealing a necklace and a bracelet worth $375,000 from the Duchess of York, Sarah Ferguson.

Judge Raymond Dearie of U.S. District Court in the New York City borough of Brooklyn told Gilbert Terrero that for the first three years of his sentence, he must perform 25 hours of community service a week.

Terrero mumbled an apology to "Miss Ferguson" and said that when he took the diamond-studded jewelry from an unlocked case in a cargo hold at John F. Kennedy International Airport in December 1995, he had no idea who it belonged to or what it was worth.
Both pieces were gifts to the Duchess from Queen Elizabeth II.
"When I found out whose it was the next day, I went to the shop steward and told him 'it was me, I want to give it back,'" said a nervous Terrero, who pleaded guilty to the theft last March.
Terrero, who appeared in court wearing a neckbrace as a result of a car accident two months ago, had faced a maximum of 12 to 18 months in jail under the sentencing guidelines.
Dearie called the theft "an amateur attempt" and "near comical," but nevertheless wanted the sentence to be a deterrent to other "opportunistic crimes" at Kennedy.
"I worry about others who work in that environment -- someone throwing an unzipped bag into a cargo hold and helping themselves to jewelry. Something about that is troubling to me," he said.
The necklace was recovered from a doghouse behind Terrero's New York City home and the bracelet was found in an airport locker. Both pieces had been broken, officials said.
